_comment: Candidate-specific packaging manifest for the Frontera runtime. Produced by P0-PKG-08, which repinned this repository's @aoc/protocol validation input from the BURNED 0.2.0-rc.0 candidate to the repaired 0.2.0-rc.1 successor. It records the identity of a produced artifact and authorizes nothing: no registry publication, no tag, no GitHub Release, no merge. release/RELEASE_MANIFEST.json is a separate machine-generated file and is not this document. Supersedes release/frontera-candidate-manifest-1.2.0.json, which is retained unchanged: 1.2.0 is not defective, and rewriting its record would falsify the evidence that it was validated against the input it was actually validated against.
source_commit_note: The last commit that affects the packed artifact. The closure commit that follows it writes only enterprise-integration.lock.json and this manifest, neither of which ships inside the tarball: `files` is ["dist"], and the packed entries outside dist/ and the bundled internals are exactly package.json, README.md and LICENSE. This is the same attribution rule the 1.2.0 manifest applied to its own evidence-only follow-ups. bbce6472 is an amend of 4b896999, which differed only in tests/protocol-canonicalization-regression.test.mjs -- not a packed path -- so both commits produce this identical artifact.
exports_fingerprint_note: RECOMPUTED from the packed artifact's own package.json (sha256 over the canonically ordered [key, target] pairs of the `exports` object), not carried forward by hand. It equals the value recorded for 1.2.0, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0. This discharges the standing caveat those manifests carried -- that no script in this repository recomputed the value -- for this increment.
http_surface_note: release/api-surface.v1.json is byte-identical across this increment (sha256 a644d8317afaa47489d60cc14d2a94bb4422d438bd72d351823f996d00b361c9): 10 route literals, 13 route patterns, 1 route prefix guard, 9 passport actions, 34 probes. scripts/check-api-freeze.mjs passes. This repin adds no route and widens no API.
protocol_exports_fingerprint_note: Unchanged from 0.2.0-rc.0. The repaired candidate moved canonicalization behaviour, not the public export map (15 keys). Recomputed two ways: from the packed rc.1 artifact's own package.json, and with Protocol's own scripts/fingerprint-public-surface.mjs at the pinned source commit.
protocol_reproduction: Repacked here from the pinned source commit through this repository's governed tool, scripts/protocol/build-protocol-tarball.mjs, in a clean shallow clone on a genuine ext4 filesystem rather than the /mnt/c DrvFs mount (DrvFs alters tar metadata). AOC_PROTOCOL_REF was set so the tool's own assertCommitMatches validated HEAD. The resulting sha256 and npm integrity both equal the authorized values exactly.
license: UNLICENSED (proprietary; LICENSE ships in the tarball)

verification_results.battery: Full final-tree battery, 21 gates, run from the frozen tree. Recorded from the run and re-confirmed by a second complete run before the closure commit.
verification_results.check:protocol-canonicalization: PASS (new in this increment; 16 checks against the INSTALLED @aoc/protocol via its public ./canonical export)
verification_results.check:clean-room-consumer: PASS (10 exports, 5 negative imports; deep and undeclared specifiers unresolvable for both @aoc-enterprise/runtime and @aoc/protocol)
verification_results.protocol:tarball:verify-lock: PASS (against the rc.1 build-result descriptor; the script requires that argument and exits 1 with a usage error if run bare, which is not a gate failure)
verification_results.protocol:tarball:validate: PASS (14 of 14 steps, exitCode 0; requires the tarball path or AOC_PROTOCOL_TARBALL)
verification_results.validate:v1-release: PASS (exit 0, including check-api-freeze, verify-release-manifest, check-release-docs, check-sdk-surface and check:portability-smoke)
verification_results.legal:check:strict: PRE-EXISTING FAIL (busboy@1.6.0, streamsearch@1.1.0 carry no recorded license in package-lock.json). Pre-existing by construction: this increment adds and removes no runtime dependency, so the finding cannot originate here. It is not part of validate:release or validate:v1-release and does not gate this artifact, which is the disposition the 1.2.0 manifest also recorded.

canonicalization_repair_proof.method: Through the INSTALLED artifact resolved by this repository own node_modules/@aoc/protocol, via the declared public ./canonical export, not by reading upstream source.
canonicalization_repair_proof.never_rc0_guard: An inequality against the literal burned version, so it cannot mutate into a passing assertion when the pin moves.

why_this_version.summary: 1.2.1 is a PATCH derived by artifact identity, not by new semantics.
why_this_version.isolated_control: Packed in clean POSIX (ext4), never on /mnt/c. Control A = base commit a937cfb4 untouched, which reproduced the RECORDED 1.2.0 artifact byte-for-byte (sha256 1b59c63d..., 3390079 bytes) -- establishing the environment as canonical, so a later difference is real and not a filesystem artifact. Control B = the same commit with ONLY the rc.0 -> rc.1 devDependency applied and the version deliberately held at 1.2.0: sha256 4fce3405d7b753a945e642eb361b0c53e5ba051da9a31937f51c134992df232f, identical 3390079 bytes, DIFFERENT CONTENT. Unpacked, A and B have 6366 entries and an identical file list, and exactly one file differs: package/package.json, at exactly one line -- the @aoc/protocol devDependency spec.
why_this_version.why_the_bytes_move: package.json ships inside the tarball and carries the `file:` devDependency spec, so repinning the peer input changes the artifact even though no compiled output does.
why_this_version.why_reuse_is_unavailable: An immutable 1.2.0 artifact exists and is consumed downstream: PMFreak vendors aoc-enterprise-runtime-1.2.0.tgz and pins it by SHA-256 1b59c63d... in vendor/aoc-consumer.lock.json, against mergeCommit a937cfb4. Reusing 1.2.0 for different bytes would make one declared version name two distinct artifacts, one of which a downstream consumer has already pinned.
why_this_version.why_the_1_0_0_precedent_does_not_extend: docs/release/FRONTERA_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_1.0.0.md held the version constant across changes to dependencies and to the @aoc/protocol devDependency -- the same class of change. Its reason was conditional: 'no immutable 1.0.0 artifact exists anywhere to conflict with.' That precondition is now false. The precedent's own reasoning is what mandates the bump.
why_this_version.semver_basis: Under this project's SemVer contract (public HTTP API surface, exported package entrypoints, store schema identifiers -- docs/enterprise/API_STABILITY_V1.md) none of the three moved. Neither breaking nor an additive public capability, therefore a patch.

reproducibility.method: Two independent reproductions by two separate sessions, each a fresh clone detached at source_commit on a POSIX (ext4) filesystem, each npm ci + npm run build + npm pack. Identical sha256, sha512, npm integrity, size (3390104) and entry count (6366).

supersedes.not_defective: 1.2.0 is NOT defective and is not withdrawn for any fault of its own. Its compiled output is byte-identical to this artifact's. What the burn invalidated is its COMPATIBILITY EVIDENCE: it was validated and handed off against @aoc/protocol@0.2.0-rc.0, an input later declared burned for a canonicalization defect. The artifact is sound; the evidence behind it was taken against a retracted input.
supersedes.burn_reason: UG-003. canonicalizeJSON truncated the exponent of numbers rendered in exponential notation with a fractional mantissa, so canonicalizeJSON(7.9e-10) and canonicalizeJSON(7.9e-100) both produced "7.9e-1": two distinct values, one canonical form, one digest. The collision is wider than the reported pair -- 1.5e-300 collapsed to "1.5e-3". Any record whose integrity rests on a canonical digest inherits the collision.
supersedes.downstream_consumption: PMFreak vendors this exact artifact and pins it by SHA-256 in vendor/aoc-consumer.lock.json.

pmfreak_integration_status: NOT_PERFORMED_IN_THIS_INCREMENT -- PMFreak still consumes 1.2.0 against the burned rc.0 input. Repinning it to this successor is downstream work this increment neither performs nor authorizes.
